proposal.blind_spot: For kernels where DRAM sits at 66-83% (not saturated) the current metrics cannot reveal whether warps are stalled on global-memory latency due to low achieved occupancy or low per-thread memory-level parallelism, so the optimizer cannot choose between raising occupancy/MLP and reducing bytes.

rationale.smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard: HIGH -> warps wait on global loads while DRAM has headroom: increase memory-level parallelism (multiple independent loads per thread, vectorized float4 loads, prefetch/unroll) rather than trimming bytes; LOW -> not latency-stalled, truly throughput-bound: reduce DRAM traffic by fusing passes and eliminating materialized intermediates (expanded bias, .contiguous() copies).
rationale.sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustain: LOW -> too few resident warps to hide latency: raise occupancy by reducing registers per thread or retuning block size/num_warps; HIGH -> occupancy is adequate: skip register/block tuning and instead add per-thread ILP with independent, wider loads.
